headline: A map-maker who kept ending up in the classroom.
lead: I came to mountains through numbers, and to teaching through patience.
paragraphs: I'm based in Patan, in the Kathmandu Valley, and I'm studying for an MSc in Mountain and Mountaineering Science at NATHM. My work sits where terrain meets water: GIS, remote sensing and hydrology applied to flood hazards and river basins in Nepal.

I also teach. For several years I've tutored A-Level students in Mathematics and Physics, and more recently IB. I care less about reciting methods than about the moment a student sees why a method works.

Outside the classroom I'm a certified trekking guide and a Balboa dance teacher. Both ask you to read a surface, a trail or a dance floor, and move carefully across it with other people. I lived in Germany for several years before returning to Nepal, and I still speak conversational German.
Online I go by BistaKaji, the name I use for games and tech reviews.

principles.title: Start from the terrain
principles.text: Look at what is actually there before deciding what it means. In research, in teaching and on the trail.

principles.title: Say what the data cannot say
principles.text: Separate what is established from what is merely plausible. It makes research more honest, and students more confident.

principles.title: Small steps, well connected
principles.text: Balboa teaches this literally. Precision at a small scale carries you through fast music, and through difficult mathematics.
